stem:
Omar has a $9$ by $4$ rectangular grid of small squares. He wants to know whether the total number of small squares is even or odd without multiplying $9 \times 4$.

Which claim correctly decides that parity?

options.text: The total is even, because one side length is even.
The answer is the tall count $9$.
The total is odd, because $9$ is odd.
The same parity rule also settles the perimeter length of the grid.

teacher.key_rationale: The product is odd only when both dimensions are odd. Here 4 is even, so the total is even without multiplying. Naming the tall count, treating one odd side as enough, or applying the rule to perimeter all miss that test.
